claims.text: The initial as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloys have a relatively coarse, suboptimally spaced dual-phase microstructure.
Controlled rapid solidification can refine the lamellar or interconnected dual-phase microstructure of eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Controlled rapid solidification can enhance phase connectivity in the dual-phase microstructure.
Adjusting the cooling rate can produce a fine-scale, optimized lamellar or interconnected architecture.
Rapid cooling produces a finer and more uniform distribution of constituent phases.
The finer phase distribution impedes dislocation movement.
Impeded dislocation movement increases yield strength.
A finer and more uniform phase distribution promotes more homogeneous stress distribution between phases.
A finer and more uniform phase distribution reduces stress concentrations between phases.
More homogeneous stress distribution and reduced interphase stress concentrations improve ductility.
Controlled rapid solidification will increase room-temperature tensile strength relative to conventional as-cast or standard thermally processed samples.
Controlled rapid solidification will increase room-temperature elongation to failure relative to conventional as-cast or standard thermally processed samples.
The simultaneous strength and ductility improvement is expected to hold under ambient, room-temperature structural loading conditions.
The proposed improvement may not extend to substantially different temperatures or to compositions outside the eutectic high-entropy alloy system studied.
